terms.meaning: the internal code that identifies one match
the batsman currently facing the bowler
a set of six legal balls bowled by one bowler
a function passed in by a parent component, run when something happens

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports
sections.what: Marks the file as browser code and brings in React tools and three icons.
sections.why: Likely reason: same pattern as the other live score pieces.

sections.name: LiveData
sections.title: Shape of live data
sections.what: Describes what the card expects: score text, status, this over's balls, two batsmen, the bowler, the next batsman and the last update time.
sections.why: Describes the server reply so the card knows its fields.
sections.watch_out: The card reads these fields directly, so a missing field can break the display.

sections.name: LiveScoreWidget (part 1)
sections.title: Fetching, refresh timer and ball colours
sections.what: Loads the match data, then refreshes every 10 seconds while auto refresh is on. Also maps each ball result to a colour: wicket red, four blue, six green, dot grey, wide or no-ball yellow, and others neutral.
sections.why: Likely reason: a quick feed that reflects each ball as it is bowled.
sections.watch_out: The refresh timer keeps the function from the first setup, so a changed matchId may keep fetching the old match.

sections.name: LiveScoreWidget (part 2)
sections.title: Card header, score and batsmen
sections.what: Shows a live label, a refresh button, an auto toggle, the score, the status, the two batsmen with the striker marked, and the bowler's figures.
sections.why: Likely reason: the key facts are visible at a glance.
sections.watch_out: Names are shortened to their last word, so a name with a suffix shows the wrong word.

sections.name: LiveScoreWidget (part 3)
sections.title: This over and footer
sections.what: Shows the balls of the current over as coloured circles, then a footer with the source, the update time and a full scorecard button when a parent supplies an action.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the visitor see the over and open the full details.
sections.watch_out: The expand button appears only when a parent passes an action in.

summary: A compact live score card for one match that refreshes every 10 seconds and can open a full scorecard.
purpose: Shows the current score, the two batsmen at the crease, the current bowler and the balls of the current over for a chosen match.
why: Reason for having a separate compact card is not stated in the code. The 10-second refresh is visible in the code.
how: 1. Loads match data from /api/live-score using the match id. 2. Repeats the load every 10 seconds while auto refresh is on. 3. Shows a connecting message until data arrives. 4. Draws the score, status, batsmen with the striker marked, bowler figures, this over's balls coloured by result, and a footer with source, update time and an optional expand button.
inputs: The matchId prop, an optional onExpand action from the parent, and the endpoint reply.
outputs: A score card and, when provided, a call to the parent's expand action.
risks: The refresh is set up once per auto refresh change, so a new matchId may keep fetching the old match. Errors are only logged, so the card can remain on connecting with no message. Fields such as the recent balls list are read without checks.
debug: If the wrong match shows after switching, check the matchId passed in and the refresh setup. If the card stays on connecting, check the browser console for the logged error and the endpoint reply.
